lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Jordan! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How's your energy been this week?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the band exercises went this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A lot of people do the band exercises while they watch TV. It makes it feel like less of a chore.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A lot of people do the band exercises while they watch TV. It makes it feel like less of a chore.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the band exercises. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A lot of people do the band exercises while they watch TV. It makes it feel like less of a chore.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to do the band exercises 5 times next week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Jordan. You're doing great.

tags.note: Notes arm strength gains; a change cue.
Warning about health consequences; pressures without permission.
Resistance to being told what to do.
Supplies an excuse the participant did not state.
Verbatim repeat of line 10; ignores prior response.
Adds 'start small' meaning not previously stated.
Expresses confidence and past success; key change talk.
Reframes goal as life-changing; pushes meaning.
Weak affirmation; unclear what effort is praised.
Sets 5-times goal without asking participant's input.
Requests later time due to appointment.

flags.reason: Warns of health decline to pressure the participant; MI non-adherent.
Same band-while-TV suggestion repeated verbatim (lines 10, 17, 31) without permission or response to participant.
Participant states confidence and past success; coach did not explore or reflect it.
Noted arm strength gains; coach moved on to a warning instead of reinforcing.
Coach set 5 sessions without collaboration after participant expressed fatigue and ambivalence.
Participant asked to reschedule; coach did not acknowledge or adjust the call timing.

score.summary: The coach repeated the same band-exercise tip three times and used warnings and an imposed 5-session goal, which pushed against the participant's stated fatigue and ambivalence. Real change talk ('My arms feel stronger', 'I know I can do it') went unexplored, and the participant's request to reschedule was not addressed.
strengths: Line 29 complex reflection captured the participant's openness and wish for the plan to fit real life.
Line 8 asked permission before sharing an idea.
Line 3 and line 6 used open questions to start the check-in.
Line 35 set a clear next contact.
coaching_tips: Replace the repeated TV tip at line 17 with an open question about what would fit the participant's energy, e.g., 'What would make these easier to fit in?'
Reflect the change talk at line 20 ('I know I can do it, I did it before') and ask what helped last time.
Remove the threat at line 12 and use reflection instead, e.g., 'Sounds like keeping your strength matters, and tiredness is getting in the way.'
Offer to set the goal together at line 33, e.g., 'What number feels realistic for next week?'
Acknowledge the reschedule request at line 36 and offer options before closing.
